environment.description: Same NestJS microservice on EKS 1.28 us-east-1. Pod uses IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) with projected token volume (audience-bound, 15min expiry). Secrets Manager automatic rotation configured with Lambda rotator on 60-second schedule via custom RotationRules (AutomaticallyAfterDays: 0, Duration: 1m, ScheduleExpression: rate(1 minute)). The rotator invalidates previous version immediately (AWSPREVIOUS deleted within rotation Lambda). Node-level IMDSv2 enforced (HttpTokens: required) but that's incidental. Cilium CNI with DNS-aware network policy: egress from the pod's namespace restricted via CiliumNetworkPolicy with toFQDNs matchPattern allowing only '*.callbacks.company.io' on port 443, with DNS proxy intercepting all UDP/53 and caching responses with a pinned TTL override of 0 (no caching, but re-resolution happens against the same authoritative response within the Cilium DNS proxy's connection-tracking window). Additionally, the pod's resolv.conf points to Cilium's DNS proxy (not CoreDNS directly), which maintains a mapping of FQDN->IP that was allowed at connection time and blocks any subsequent connections to IPs not matching the original resolution for that FQDN within the same flow context.
